case-1.objects: Types α and β, their measurable-space structures, measures μ on α and ν on β, and the product measure μ.prod ν on α × β. In the definition, γ denotes a generic measure on α × β; in the example it is instantiated by μ.prod ν.
case-1.domains: The measures μ and ν live on the given measurable spaces α and β, respectively. μ.prod ν lives on α × β with the product measurable-space structure. The first and second projections go from α × β to α and β, respectively.
case-1.quantifiers: For all implicit types α and β and all supplied measurable-space instances on them, and for all measures μ : Measure α and ν : Measure β supplied explicitly, the proposition holds under the two implicit probability-measure instances. The example does not quantify over a separate candidate coupling γ.
case-1.assumptions: There are instances [MeasurableSpace α] and [MeasurableSpace β], and instances [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] and [IsProbabilityMeasure ν]. The latter state that μ and ν each give mass one to the whole of their respective spaces. No further hypothesis is explicit.
case-1.conclusion: IsCoupling (μ.prod ν) μ ν; unfolding IsCoupling, (μ.prod ν).fst = μ ∧ (μ.prod ν).snd = ν.
case-1.senses: The two conjuncts are equalities of measures: pushing the product measure forward along the first projection recovers μ, and pushing it forward along the second recovers ν. The assertion identifies the product measure as a coupling; it does not assert uniqueness, characterize all couplings, or state that every coupling is a product measure. The rectangle mass formula is background for the product measure, not a separate conclusion.
case-1.constants: The named notions and operations are MeasurableSpace, Measure, IsProbabilityMeasure, Measure.prod, Measure.fst, Measure.snd, and the defined predicate IsCoupling, with equality and conjunction in its body. The normalization constant is 1 in each probability assumption; there are no fixed choices of types or measures and no other numerical constants.
